Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c40b6e10091fa528d6c7ff6f6fe1d020848d6eee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md + none (the diff carries no file that implements or enforces the sentence; the cited code was READ on main b63c8949, never reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/function-package-scope.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts). The changeset is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Card #32522 (Part of epic #31527). Net diff against main: 2 files, +14 / -4, head 1 ahead and 14 behind main; no main commit since the merge base 6538ba48 touches either path. The cited code moved on main since 6538ba48 (registry.ts, service-automation engine.ts), so every line below was read on main b63c8949, not on the base.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: no change. The diff touches no schema, no runtime code, no gate. Right.
- Public surface: the published `@objectstack/skills` catalog (skills/** ships there) changes one paragraph of `objectstack-automation`, item 3 of "Valid-but-silently-wrong". Right: it is the stale line card #32522 names, and the rewrite now matches the narrowing #32513 (card #31700) shipped.
- Evals: no eval under skills/ asserts the old sentence (`git grep` on main for `Bare-name conflict`, `normalize_phone`, `acme.sales`, `the platform's counts` hits only this paragraph and the package CHANGELOG). No other skill teaches the function one-holder rule. Right: no eval was owed.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/32522-skills-automation-function-name-per-namespace.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, the same shape as the sibling skills-docs changeset on main (33235). A prose correction in the catalog is a patch. Right.
- `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right: no accept set, published schema, wire answer or behaviour moves; the sentence follows behaviour #32513 already declared.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none.
- Dev deviations, each answered:
  - Signature as a plain line, not an HTML-comment marker; no assignees. Process only, nothing in the tree. Accepted.
  - Ran below the mandated tier; the contract review at tier is owed before landing. This record is that review.
  - The card's premise re-check (zero hits for `Bare-name conflict at boot` means close) does not apply as written. Agreed: on main the warning still fires for a pair that meets (one namespace, or a package with none), so the string stays, scoped to that pair. The premise held: the old line said every two-package pair warns.
  - Branch not merged with main (14 behind). No conflict, no overlapping path, and the cited code still holds on main b63c8949 (④). Accepted.
- Card Fix paragraph, third item ("what a two-holder bare engine read answers (ruling R2-C)"): not written into the skill. Graded N2 below and accepted as a deviation.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`, lines 268 to 271, new sentence: "Packages of two `namespace`s each run their own `normalize_phone` (one namespace, or none: refused at install; a boot warns `Bare-name conflict at boot`). If the flow's package holds none, two holders in reach or one only outside its `dependencies` closure fail the step as a guard ..."

Checked clause by clause against main b63c8949:

1. "Packages of two `namespace`s": `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` (packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts:156) lists `'function'` (the picklist family, #31700). objectql `bareNameHoldersMeet` (bare-name-one-holder.ts:424) returns true for any type not on that list, else `namespacedHoldersMeet` (spec namespace-prefix.ts:220): two holders meet unless both declare a namespace and the two differ. The namespace is the installed record's `manifest.namespace` (registry.ts `bareNameHolderNamespace`). `function` has no built-in name (`BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES.function` is empty) and is not package-scoped, so the platform-requested-name exception never applies. The skill's partition (two namespaces apart; one namespace, or none, together) is exactly the meeting set. The mixed pair (one declares, one does not) lands in "refused" under either reading of "one namespace, or none", as the code has it. Holds.
2. "each run their own": a flow `script` node resolves through `AutomationEngine.resolveFunction(name, context)` (service-automation engine.ts:4663), with the calling flow's armed package as the caller, into `functionResolverOf` and objectql `resolvePackageScopedFunction` (package-scoped-resolver.ts:200) over `functionHoldersOf`, which keeps every holder per package. A packaged flow runs its own package's function first (function-package-scope.ts module doc; screen-nodes.ts:653). Holds.
3. "refused at install": `claimBareNameFunctions` (registry.ts:5444) throws `BareNameConflictError` (`422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`) once sealed, for a bind bringing a function a meeting package holds, ahead of any registration; a holder of another namespace is skipped (`bareNameHoldersOtherThan`, `bareNameHoldersMeet`). Holds; see N1 on the word "install".
4. "a boot warns `Bare-name conflict at boot`": `sealBareNameHolders` (registry.ts:5525) reports each later holder only against an earlier one it meets, and `sealBareNameHoldersAtColdBoot` (registry.ts:3014) under `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE = 'warn'` (bare-name-one-holder.ts:466) logs `bareNameColdBootWarning` (registry.ts:2933), whose text opens "Bare-name conflict at boot:". Two namespaces' holders produce no conflict and no warning. Holds.
5. "If the flow's package holds none, two holders in reach or one only outside its `dependencies` closure fail the step as a guard": unchanged except that "(the platform's counts)" is dropped. The sentence before still puts the platform's owner-less function "in every flow's reach", and `resolvePackageScopedFunction`'s doc says a package caller holding none "counts it beside its closure's holders", so "two holders in reach" still covers the platform. The guard (`code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'`, no `fault` edge, `innerRefusal`) matches screen-nodes.ts:651 to 660. Holds.

Ruling R2-C (epic seat ruling 6812862622, posted on #31700 for epic #31527), quoted: "When two namespaces hold a function name, `resolveFunction` / `resolveFunctionEntry` refuse it as ambiguous, naming both holders; a one-holder name resolves as before." On main that is objectql engine.ts:772 and :787 (`PackageScopedNameRefusedError`, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`). It governs the BARE engine read, the call that names no package. No flow path reaches it: the `script` node always passes the flow's context. The only other caller on main, the runtime binder (app-artifact-handlers.ts:595), reads it only when one package holds the name. So R2-C does not govern the skill's sentence, and the sentence does not contradict it.

Trying to break it: (a) the one-namespace pair at boot. The warning changes nothing about which holder each caller is served, and the engine keeps both holders, so each flow still runs its own function. The new sentence says only "a boot warns", which is true; it claims no refusal at boot. (b) A no-namespace package beside a namespaced holder: both meet, so the bind is refused, as the parenthetical says. (c) Two namespaces where the flow's package holds none and both are in its closure: two holders in reach, guard refusal, as the next sentence says. No break found.

Findings:

- N1, nit: "refused at install". For a function the refusing door is the hook binder's bind (`bindHooksToEngine`, hook-binder.ts:221), not the package's install. On the runtime binder that throw is caught and logged at `error` ("Failed to bind declarative hooks", app-artifact-handlers.ts, which never throws), so that owner group's hooks and functions stay unbound while the package itself installs. The wording matches the platform's own warning text ("a further package declaring the name is refused at install"), and the remedy an author needs (rename, or declare another namespace) is the same. No effect on correctness. Accepted deviation; no fix.
- N2, nit: the card's Fix asks the rewrite to say "what a two-holder bare engine read answers (ruling R2-C)". The skill leaves this out on purpose: its reader writes `script` nodes, which never reach the bare read (above). The tree is right to leave it out. The PR body's line that the flow guard refusal "is already the flow-level face of ruling R2-C" is not accurate: that refusal comes from the package-scoped resolver (#32073) and only shares the `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` shape. That is PR-body prose, not the tree. Accepted deviation from the card's Fix paragraph.
- N3, nit: dropping "(the platform's counts)" makes the reader infer from the sentence before that the platform's function is one of the "two holders in reach". The inference is correct and stated one clause earlier. Accepted.

Out of scope (read, not reviewed; follow-up candidate, no effect on this verdict): packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts:215 to 216 on main still says the function bind refusal "stays until the trailing backstop child (ADR-0150 D9) narrows it", but `claimBareNameFunctions` already narrows it through `bareNameHoldersMeet`. That is a stale code comment.

Since the merge, main has changed neither file this PR touched: both are byte-identical between the head and main 8e63ed87. Of the code read, only packages/objectql/src/registry.ts moved after the merge (#33463, a permission-set refusal text); everything below was read on main 8e63ed87. The earlier record 6882471862 is not used as evidence; ③ says which of its findings this review confirms.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: no change. The diff holds no schema, no runtime code and no gate. Right.
- Public surface: one paragraph of the published `@objectstack/skills` catalog, item 3 of "Valid-but-silently-wrong" in `objectstack-automation` (lines 268 to 271). Right: it is the line the card names, and the old text (every two-package pair makes the boot warn) is false on main since `function` joined `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES`.
- Evals: the two eval files of the skill assert nothing about a function name two packages hold (the one `script` eval, `pricing.recalc`, is untouched and still true). On main, `Bare-name conflict` and `normalize_phone` appear under skills/ only in this paragraph. Right: no eval was owed.
- Token ceiling: not moved; the head's gate check-runs are green.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/32522-skills-automation-function-name-per-namespace.md` declares `'@objectstack/skills': patch`. A prose correction in the shipped catalog is a patch. Right. The three Check Changeset runs on the head are success.
- `Clause-②: no` with `Metadata-protocol: none`, on the PR body and the changeset. Right: nothing the platform accepts, publishes or answers moves; the sentence follows behaviour #32513 already shipped.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the dev report 6882192431.
- Dev deviations, each answered:
  - Plain-line signature and no assignees: process only, nothing in the tree. Accepted.
  - The dev thread ran below the mandated tier and said the at-tier review was owed. The record 6882471862 did not pay it (correction 6886588421); this record does.
  - The card's premise re-check (zero hits for `Bare-name conflict at boot` means close) does not apply as written. Agreed: on main the cold boot still warns for a pair that meets, so the string stays, scoped to that pair.
  - Branch not merged with main before landing: no overlapping path, and the code holds on today's main.
- Card Fix, third item (what a two-holder bare engine read answers, ruling R2-C): not written into the skill. See N2 of the earlier record below; accepted.
- Earlier record 6882471862 (off-tier), finding by finding:
  - Its five clause checks: confirmed independently on main 8e63ed87 (④).
  - N1 ("refused at install" is really the bind): the fact is confirmed; the grade is not. This review grades it should-fix (F1).
  - N2 (R2-C bare engine read left out; the PR body's "flow-level face of R2-C" is loose): confirmed, nit. The bare read (`resolveFunction` / `resolveFunctionEntry`, pinned by the test "[epic seat ruling R2-C]") is never reached by a `script` node, which always resolves through the package-scoped resolver with the flow's package. The tree is right to omit it.
  - N3 (dropping "(the platform's counts)"): confirmed, nit (F2).
  - Its out-of-scope note on packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts: confirmed on main 8e63ed87, lines 214 to 216 still say the function bind refusal "stays until the trailing backstop child (ADR-0150 D9) narrows it", and it has narrowed. Stale code comment, outside this diff.
  - It carried no should-fix item, so there is none to check as fixed.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`, the new sentence: "Packages of two `namespace`s each run their own `normalize_phone` (one namespace, or none: refused at install; a boot warns `Bare-name conflict at boot`). If the flow's package holds none, two holders in reach or one only outside its `dependencies` closure fail the step as a guard ..."

Clause by clause, against main 8e63ed87:

1. "Packages of two `namespace`s": `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES` (core package-scoped-resolution.ts) lists `'function'`. `bareNameHoldersMeet` (objectql bare-name-one-holder.ts) answers true for a type off that list, else `namespacedHoldersMeet` (spec namespace-prefix.ts): two holders meet unless both declare a namespace and the two differ. The platform-requested-name exception is gated on `isPackageScopedType`, which the engine's function type is not, so it never applies. A holder's namespace is its installed record's `manifest.namespace`, the key an author writes. Holds.
2. "each run their own": `resolvePackageScopedHolders` step 1 returns the caller package's own item whenever it holds the name, before the closure or the platform is read; the `script` node reaches it through `functionResolverOf` and `resolvePackageScopedFunction` with the calling flow's package. The engine keeps every holder per package (test: "after the seal, two packages of two namespaces each bind a function of one name, and each keeps its own holder"). Holds.
3. "one namespace, or none": the meeting set exactly. Two packages of one namespace meet; a package with no namespace meets every holder; the mixed pair (one declares, one does not) meets and reads as refused under either reading of the phrase. Holds.
4. "refused at install": after the seal, `claimBareNameFunctions` (registry.ts) throws `BareNameConflictError` for a bind bringing a function a meeting package holds, ahead of any registration, and skips a holder of another namespace. Before the seal it only records. Holds for the bind; see F1 for "install".
5. "a boot warns `Bare-name conflict at boot`": `sealBareNameHolders` reports a later holder only against an earlier one it meets; `sealBareNameHoldersAtColdBoot` under `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE = 'warn'` logs `bareNameColdBootWarning`, whose text opens with that string. Two namespaces' holders give no conflict and no warning (test: "the cold boot of two namespaces' API and function holders boots with no bare-name warning"). Holds.
6. "If the flow's package holds none, two holders in reach or one only outside its `dependencies` closure": unchanged but for the dropped parenthesis. Step 2 of the resolver counts the platform's owner-less function beside the closure's holders and refuses `ambiguous-in-closure`; step 3 refuses `outside-closure`. Holds.

Tried to break it:
- One-namespace pair that both came through the boot: the warning changes nothing, each flow still runs its own function. The sentence claims only the warning there. No break.
- Two namespaces, the flow's package holding none and both holders in its closure: refused as the next sentence says. No break.
- A flow's own package and the platform both holding the name: step 1 runs the package's own. Consistent with "each run their own". No break.
- The post-seal bind of a one-namespace second holder: this is where the sentence is loose (F1).

Findings:

- F1, should-fix (follow-up card; the PR is merged): "refused at install" is not what happens to a function. The only door that judges a function is the hook binder's bind (`bindHooksToEngine` calls `claimBareNameFunctions`); the package door and the item seam judge registry types only, and `function` is not one (`BARE_NAME_REGISTRY_TYPES` filters it out). The runtime's one binder, `bindAppArtifactHandlers` (called from `AppPlugin.start`), catches that throw per owner group and logs it at `error` as "Failed to bind declarative hooks". So the second package INSTALLS; what is refused is the bind, and with it every function and every hook of that owner group, the non-clashing ones included (test: "registers nothing", `beta_only_fn` stays unregistered). The author then sees no install refusal at all. Its `script` node fails as unregistered, or, if the package declares the first holder as a dependency, resolves step 2 and silently runs the OTHER package's function. That is the opposite of the loud stop the words promise, in the skill's own "Valid-but-silently-wrong" list. It is graded should-fix and not must-fix because the sentence is a newly added claim that mis-states the symptom, while what the author is told to write (rename, or another namespace) stays right, the platform's own boot warning uses the same words, and a post-seal function bind is rare (functions are code, so only a code bundle bound after the boot reaches it). Suggested wording within the budget: say the later package's functions and hooks are not bound, logged as an error, in place of "refused at install". The file sits at its token ceiling (6861 of 6861), so the fix must pay for itself.
- F2, nit: dropping "(the platform's counts)" leaves the reader to infer from the clause before ("in every flow's reach") that the platform's function is one of the "two holders in reach". The inference is correct. Accepted deviation.
- F3, nit: the parenthesis "(one namespace, or none: refused at install; a boot warns ...)" compresses two different moments (a new holder after the boot; a pair already held at the boot) into one clause, and a reader can take both to happen together. Accepted deviation; fold into the F1 card if that sentence is rewritten.

Outside the diff, read and not reviewed, follow-up candidates with no effect on this verdict: the stale comment at packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts lines 214 to 216; and `bareNameColdBootWarning` in packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, whose generic "refused at install" text is the source of F1's wording and is equally loose for a function.
